# A folded prior SNAPSHOT is not a lost event

`fsck_repair.snapshot_missing_sources` flags any cited `source_event_uuids` entry with no
file on disk. But when compaction folds a ticket, the SUPERSEDED SNAPSHOT is itself listed as
a source of its successor, and that snapshot file is then legitimately gone — consumed. No
data is lost: a snapshot's entire content IS its `compiled_state`, which the successor
absorbed.

Treating that as an incomplete log is wrong twice over: it reports a healthy ticket as
damaged, and (post b636) it makes the ticket look un-rebuildable.

## Evidence
After the b636 remediation, 6 tickets still report SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES:
316c-6c42-32d3-4f9b, a6ea-6a28-1d84-4626, bbc0-1dbd-d9cb-4917, be08-b46d-51be-419d,
c7c5-12ea-ad68-4690, e0d4-4f19-699d-4d61.
Each is missing EXACTLY ONE uuid, and in every case that uuid resolves (via the path it was
added at in tickets history) to a `-SNAPSHOT.json` event. All six reduce to `closed`
correctly — their state is intact. The 7th (f130) was a genuine EDIT loss and was repaired
separately.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `snapshot_missing_sources` does NOT count a cited uuid whose event is a SNAPSHOT
      superseded by the citing snapshot. Determine the type without a history walk where
      possible (the reducer/compaction knows which uuid was the folded snapshot).
- [x] The six tickets above report clean afterwards, with their status unchanged.
- [x] A genuinely missing raw event is still reported (no weakening of the b636 guard) —
      held-out test asserts both directions.
- [x] Consider recording the folded snapshot uuid distinctly in the SNAPSHOT payload so the
      distinction is structural rather than inferred.
